cons.vote_default: No agreement on {decision}: {option} applies by default
cons.why.cannibal_fault: A donor system keeps working with fewer spares and lower reliability: the repair works today and creates the next failure.
cons.why.conflict_aftermath: A decision nobody shares does not remove the conflict; it comes back with the next small mistake.
cons.why.food_illness: Bacteria and their toxins take hours or days to act: the meal looked and tasted normal, so only the symptoms reveal the contamination.
cons.why.food_poisoning: Bacteria need hours to multiply inside the body: the crew feels fine at the table and ill a few days later.
cons.why.generic: Every decision leaves a trace that comes back later with its own timing.
cons.why.power_fault: A cell that works at its limit overheats again; lowering the load does not repair it, it only delays the failure.
cons.why.pressure_seal: The seal was replaced with a part from the wrong batch.
cons.why.pump_failure: The pump was overhauled in a hurry, without spare seals.
cons.why.radiation_dose: Living cells accumulate damage from charged particles; the effect appears days later, when the dose already happened.
cons.why.vote_default: When the votes split, the default option runs anyway and nobody feels responsible for it: efficiency and trust drop for a couple of days.
cons.why.waste_vent: Organic waste was pressed through a vent meant for air.
decision.disable.opt.disable.why: With no power draw there is no data: the energy saved today is measured against the samples the mission will never collect.
decision.disable.opt.keep.estimate: No science lost, more power drawn
decision.disable.opt.keep.why: Every instrument draws power and heat while it runs; keeping them all on protects the science objectives but eats the generation margin.
decision.orbit.opt.shift.estimate: New coverage, −12 M€ and attitude stress
decision.orbit.opt.shift.why: Changing orbit means burning propellant and money, and the attitude system pays for the manoeuvre; the reward is geometry that reaches new ground tracks.
decision.orbit.opt.stay.estimate: No cost, same coverage and same transmission windows
decision.orbit.opt.stay.why: An orbit is a balance of height and speed: staying keeps the coverage you already have and spends nothing, but gains nothing new either.
decision.ration.opt.full.estimate: Hunger eases, morale rises, food runs out sooner
decision.ration.opt.full.why: A full portion covers the energy the body needs for the day, but every full meal spends stores that later days will miss.
decision.ration.opt.half.estimate: Food lasts longer, but hunger, stress and morale suffer
decision.ration.opt.half.why: Splitting the portion stretches the pantry, yet the body still needs the missing calories: hunger grows, sleep worsens and stress climbs.
decision.transmit.opt.burst.estimate: Data leaves now, comms wear and −6 M€
decision.transmit.opt.burst.why: Transmitting outside the window pushes the antenna and the power budget past their comfort zone: the signal gets out, but the hardware pays for it.
decision.transmit.opt.wait.estimate: No cost, the data stays on board
decision.transmit.opt.wait.why: A ground station only hears the ship when the antenna and the station line up; waiting costs nothing, but the data stays stored and at risk.

event.ev.battery_failure.description: One cell of the battery bank heats up and drops out. Stored energy falls and the bus is no longer stable.
event.ev.battery_failure.opt.load_shed.e: Power serviced, warmer ship, lower morale and a pending fault
event.ev.battery_failure.opt.load_shed.w: Cutting the load hides the fault instead of repairing it: the thermal loop works harder and the damaged cell may fail again days later.
event.ev.battery_failure.opt.swap_bank.e: Power repaired and money spent, plus a tense shift
event.ev.battery_failure.opt.swap_bank.w: A spare cell restores capacity immediately; the parts come out of the operations budget and the crew has to work in a hurry.
event.ev.battery_failure.title: Battery failure
event.ev.comms_blackout.description: The antenna points correctly but the signal does not lock. The window closes in minutes.
event.ev.comms_blackout.opt.low_gain.why: A wider beam needs less accuracy and saves the window, but it is slow: part of the queue will not go out.
event.ev.comms_blackout.opt.repair_windo: Link repaired, tired crew and money spent
Repair the feed during the window
Working on the antenna while it is visible repairs the real cause, but the crew works without rest and the spare parts cost money.
event.ev.comms_blackout.title: Communications blackout
event.ev.crew_conflict.description: Two crew members refuse to work together after a mistake in the laboratory. The shift cannot be covered.
event.ev.crew_conflict.opt.commander_dec: Schedule kept, morale down and a grudge for later
A decision closes the shift on time and keeps the data flowing, but a decision nobody shares leaves tension that returns days later.
event.ev.crew_conflict.opt.mediate.estim: Less rest and a small cost, but morale recovers
event.ev.crew_conflict.opt.mediate.label: Mediate and split the shift
event.ev.crew_conflict.opt.mediate.why: Mediation repairs the working relationship and the crew pulls together, but it takes hours out of the sleep budget.
event.ev.crew_conflict.title: Crew conflict
event.ev.earth_request.description: The control centre asks for the latest measurements. The next window is short and the memory is almost full.
Data spent, money credited and a crew on edge
Send the priority data in the first window
The first window is short, so you can only send part of the data; the agency pays for what it receives, but the crew must choose what to drop.
event.ev.earth_request.opt.late_window.e: Less data lost, morale down and antenna wear
event.ev.earth_request.opt.late_window.l: Wait for the next window and send more
event.ev.earth_request.opt.late_window.w: Waiting lets you send a better selection with less loss, but the answer from Earth arrives late and the crew feels abandoned.
event.ev.earth_request.title: Request from Earth
event.ev.food_outbreak.description: The galley reports a sour smell. Part of the stock is below fifty-five percent freshness and someone already feels queasy.
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.cook_clean.es: Freshness recovers a little, water and money spent
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.cook_clean.la: Cook it thoroughly and clean the galley
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.cook_clean.wh: Heat kills most bacteria, so cooking buys time; cleaning uses water and supplies, and the value already lost cannot be recovered.
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.discard.estim: Waste and lower morale, but the rest of the pantry recovers
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.discard.label: Discard the spoiled stock
event.ev.food_outbreak.opt.discard.why: Throwing the bad units away removes the source of the problem: the pantry loses quantity and the crew complains, but nothing else spoils.
Illness now, money saved and a bill to pay later
Eating spoiled food is a probability, not a certainty: you save the cost of a replacement, but the crew gets sick and the damage returns days later.
event.ev.food_outbreak.title: Food outbreak
event.ev.isolation.description: The crew has been far from home for weeks. Arguments over small things and long silences begin.
event.ev.isolation.opt.group_session.est: Stress down and morale up, but less rest
event.ev.isolation.opt.group_session.why: Talking about the problem lowers stress and raises morale; the price is sleep, which is also a resource.
event.ev.isolation.opt.private_time.why: Privacy helps without meetings, but the schedule slips and some measurements wait for the next window.
event.ev.isolation.title: Isolation
event.ev.micrometeorites.description: A cloud of dust and small debris crosses the orbit. At this speed a grain of sand hits like a bullet.
event.ev.micrometeorites.opt.absorb.esti: Optics and thermal loop worn down
event.ev.micrometeorites.opt.absorb.labe: Hold the attitude and take the hits
event.ev.micrometeorites.opt.absorb.why: Small debris rarely breaks the hull, but it pits the optics and the radiators; the crew spends nothing and keeps the schedule.
event.ev.micrometeorites.opt.maneuver.es: Attitude wear, money spent and broken sleep
event.ev.micrometeorites.opt.maneuver.wh: Changing the orbit avoids the impacts; the cost is propellant and a night without rest.
event.ev.micrometeorites.title: Micrometeorites
event.ev.overheating.description: The thermal loop cannot dump heat fast enough and the laboratory goes past its limit.
More coolant flow and a wider radiator area remove the heat, but the pumps eat the power the instruments need.
event.ev.overheating.opt.throttle_instru: Instruments worn, data lost and crew stress up
Producing less heat is free in money and expensive in science: the instruments work below their design point and lose measurements.
event.ev.overheating.title: Overheating
event.ev.pressure_leak.description: A seal fails in the laboratory module. Air escapes slowly and the loop cannot keep up.
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.isolate.estim: Life support damaged, samples and morale lost
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.isolate.label: Isolate and vent the module
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.isolate.why: Closing the module stops the leak at once and is the safest option for the crew, but the samples stored there are lost.
Money saved, but the crew risks falling ill
Keep working and monitor the pressure
A slow leak is survivable for a few days and saves the repair money, but the low pressure and the humidity make the crew ill.
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.patch.estimat: Life support repaired, money spent and stress up
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.patch.label: Patch the seal from outside
event.ev.pressure_leak.opt.patch.why: A patch seals the hole in minutes, but it costs a spacewalk and the sealing kit is not free.
event.ev.pressure_leak.title: Pressure leak
event.ev.solar_storm.description: A wave of charged particles reaches the ship. The radiation level outside jumps and the electronics start to fail.
Extra data now, radiation sickness in a few days
Keep the instruments on and accept the dose
A storm is also the best moment to measure particles; the price is a dose that shows up later as illness instead of immediately.
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.shelter.estimat: No dose and no cost, but observations stop and the crew sleeps badly
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.shelter.label: Shelter the crew in the core module
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.shelter.why: Water and dense walls are the best shield on board: staying inside the core adds no mass and costs nothing, but the instruments must shut down and the crew cannot rest well.
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.turn_hull.estim: Attitude wear and a charge on the budget, but morale holds
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.turn_hull.label: Turn the hull into the particle flow
event.ev.solar_storm.opt.turn_hull.why: Pointing the thickest side at the flow blocks most of the particles; the cost is propellant and manoeuvring wear, spending you cannot recover.
event.ev.solar_storm.title: Solar storm
event.ev.storm_forecast.description: Earth warns that a solar storm will reach the ship in about two days. The schedule can still be changed.
event.ev.storm_forecast.opt.observe_stor: Much more science, less rest and a risk of power damage
Plan an observation of the storm
A storm crossing the ship is a unique measurement; the crew will sleep less and part of the power system may not survive the extra load.
event.ev.storm_forecast.opt.prepare_shie: Money spent in advance, link serviced
Prepare the shelter and the link now
Two days is enough to move supplies into the core and put the antenna in a safe position: it is cheap now, and the storm finds you ready.
event.ev.storm_forecast.title: Storm forecast

glossary.budget.def: Money for components, the launch and operations. It is spent during design and also on decisions during the mission, and it does not come back.
glossary.cannibalization.def: Taking parts from one system to repair another immediately. It lowers the donor’s reliability by 15 to 25 points and schedules a breakdown in 3 to 6 days or after 5 events.
glossary.comms_window.def: The minutes in which the antenna sees Earth and data can be sent. Outside the window the data waits on board, and waiting data can be lost.
glossary.coverage.def: The share of the surface or the atmosphere that the orbit lets you observe. The objective fixes a minimum, and each orbit has its own ceiling.
glossary.data.def: What the instruments measure. It is stored in a limited memory and only gains full scientific value when it is transmitted during a window.
glossary.delta_v.def: The total change of speed a mission needs. Here it is reduced to how far the launcher can take you: a heavier ship or a higher orbit asks for more delta-v.
glossary.eclipse.def: The part of each revolution in which the body blocks the Sun. The panels stop charging, so the ship works from the battery.
glossary.freshness.def: How good the food still is. It drops about 2 % per day with a working fridge and 8 % per day with a broken one; below 30 % the risk of illness appears days later.
glossary.life_support.def: The system that keeps air, water and temperature inside the safe range. When it drops, the whole crew degrades at once, and the damage is slow to reverse.
glossary.mass.def: How much the ship and its payload weigh. The launcher can only lift a fixed maximum, so every kilogram added takes margin away from the rest.
glossary.orbit.def: The path the ship follows around the body. It decides how much ground you cover, how often you can talk to Earth, how long you spend in shadow and how much radiation you receive.
glossary.power.def: Energy the ship can generate and energy the systems and instruments consume. If consumption is higher than generation, something has to be switched off.
glossary.radiation.def: Charged particles that damage living cells. It depends on the orbit and acts slowly: the dose is received today and the effect shows up days later.
glossary.reliability.def: The chance that a system keeps working without failing. It drops with use and with every breakdown, and it is repaired with maintenance, not with repairs.
glossary.technical_debt.def: The cost of a quick fix that solves today and creates a problem tomorrow. Cannibalising a system is the clearest example: it repairs one thing and schedules a failure in another.
glossary.title: Glossary

journal.data_lost: {amount} KB of data lost: storage was full
journal.food_spoiled: Removed from the pantry as spoiled: {item}
journal.why.data_lost: Data storage is finite: when the buffer is full, new measurements overwrite or drop what was never transmitted.
journal.why.food_spoiled: Fresh food loses quality every day and faster when the fridge fails: below 30 % freshness, bacteria win the race.
journal.why.repair: Repairing restores working condition but not reliability: a part that failed once will fail again sooner.
journal.why.system_failure: Every component degrades with use: low reliability turns normal wear into a failure, and a failed system drags down everything that depends on it.

orbit.high.desc: From high orbit the ship is almost never in shadow, so the panels charge without interruption and the link is always open at moderate bandwidth. The price is worse detail, because each pass covers less ground, and the highest radiation after the transfer orbit.
orbit.high.name: High orbit
orbit.low.desc: You fly close to the surface, so the instruments see small details but each pass covers only part of the ground. The orbit lasts about ninety minutes, the link opens for ten minutes in each pass and the ship spends a third of the time in shadow, so the panels charge in cycles. Radiation is the lowest of the four.
orbit.low.name: Low orbit
orbit.medium.desc: A balanced orbit: it covers most of the surface and the passes last longer, so there are more observation opportunities. Each revolution takes about four hours, the link opens for twenty minutes with a wide bandwidth and the ship is in shadow a fifth of the time. Radiation is moderate.
orbit.medium.name: Medium orbit
orbit.transfer.desc: The long approach: the ship sweeps most of the body and transmits with the full bandwidth, but one revolution takes two days, so the ship is out of contact almost all the time. Radiation is the highest of the four and every contact has to be planned in advance.
orbit.transfer.name: Transfer orbit

report.analysis.collaboration: Collaboration rewards agreement: {agreed} of {total} votes were unanimous, and a solo mission cannot earn the full collaboration points.
report.analysis.decisions: Decisions are judged by the consequences avoided: {fired} of {scheduled} scheduled consequences fired anyway.
report.analysis.efficiency: Efficiency compares what was spent with what was available: budget {budget} %, power margin {power} % and days saved {time} %.
report.analysis.mission: The mission rubric asks how much of the objective was really delivered: {coverage} % of the requirements were covered, and a partial delivery keeps only a quarter of the points.
report.analysis.science: Science scores the measurements that reached Earth: {value} of {required} required units; data still on board counts at 60 % because it can still be lost.
report.analysis.survival: Survival mixes headcount and health: {alive} of {total} crew members alive, with health condition counting for 40 %.
report.analysis_none: Nothing was lost: every rubric is at its maximum.
report.none: There is no report yet. Fly a mission or import one.
report.title: Mission report
report.tradeoff.data_left_behind: More data stayed on board than reached Earth: storing is not delivering.
report.tradeoff.mission_vs_crew: The objective was met, but the crew paid for it: survival dropped below half.
report.tradeoff.no_agreement: No collective decision was unanimous: every default option cost efficiency and trust.
report.tradeoff.science_vs_resources: The science objectives were met at a high resource cost: good data, but the budget and power were pushed to the limit.
report.why.collaboration: Collaboration counts unanimous votes: {agreed} of {total} decisions were agreed.
report.why.decisions: Every scheduled consequence that fires takes points with it: {fired} of {scheduled} triggered.
report.why.efficiency: Half of this score comes from the budget left ({budget} %), 30 % from the power margin ({power} %) and 20 % from the days saved ({time} %).
report.why.mission_met: The objective is met and {coverage} % of the requirements are covered: the mission delivered what it promised.
report.why.mission_partial: Every requirement needs its own instrument and orbit: without them the objective closes with {coverage} % coverage.
report.why.science: Transmitted data counts in full and data left on board counts at 60 %: {value} of {required} required units.
report.why.survival: Survival weighs both the people still alive and their health: {alive} of {total} crew members made it.

scenario.scn.ceres_survey.brief: Ceres keeps water ice under a dusty crust. You need a radar map of a whole region and enough memory to store it: data is the critical resource and every transmission window counts.
scenario.scn.ceres_survey.desc: Map the surface of the dwarf planet in detail before the ice sublimates in the sunlight.
scenario.scn.ceres_survey.name: Ceres survey
scenario.scn.europa_ice.brief: The seismometer has to record the tides of the hidden ocean for weeks. Time is the critical resource: the signal only appears after a long, quiet stay, and every interruption costs science.
scenario.scn.europa_ice.desc: Listen to the ice of a moon that hides an ocean under its crust.
scenario.scn.europa_ice.name: Europa ice
scenario.scn.venus_atmosphere.brief: The cloud deck moves fast and the surface is hell. Study the atmosphere from a safe distance: power is the critical resource because the instruments and the link compete for the same energy.
scenario.scn.venus_atmosphere.desc: Measure the winds and the cloud layer of a planet that crushes anything it touches.
scenario.scn.venus_atmosphere.name: Venus atmosphere

tutorial.deferred_consequence.body: Pause the clock and open the pending consequences. Every important decision carries a trigger: it fires in a few days or after a number of events.
tutorial.deferred_consequence.title: The bill arrives later
tutorial.design_basic.body: The mission objective comes first. Read what it asks for: the list on the right marks with ✔ what you already meet and with ✘ what you still need.
tutorial.design_basic.title: Start with the objective
tutorial.first_repair.body: Open the crew actions and repair a damaged system. Repairs restore the state but not the reliability: that needs preventive maintenance.
tutorial.first_repair.title: Your first repair
tutorial.launch_check.body: The launch stays blocked until mass, orbit, budget and power fit. When it is blocked, the button explains the reason and how to fix it.
tutorial.launch_check.title: Check the launcher
tutorial.settings_hint: The tutorial only appears in Basic difficulty and in the first mission.
tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.tradeoffs.body: Switch a group to its advanced version. It usually gains performance, but mass, power, data or cost go up: look at what moves in the resource panel on the right.
tutorial.tradeoffs.title: Every piece trades something
